post.title: How a student loan can charge interest on interest
post.ig:
Your student loan can still charge interest on its own interest.

It's called capitalization: unpaid interest is added to your principal.
New undergrad Direct Loans (July 2026 to June 2027) carry a fixed 6.52%.
Hypothetical: $10,000 at 6.52%, no payments for 4 years, simple interest adds $2,608. If that interest capitalizes, say at consolidation, yearly interest goes from $652 to about $822.
Since July 2023, Direct Loans no longer capitalize when you enter repayment or leave forbearance; consolidation, some deferments ending and leaving IBR (older loans) still trigger it.

Sources: US Department of Education (Federal Register, Nov 2022; FSA, June 2026), studentaid.gov.

post.yt_desc:
Capitalization adds unpaid interest to your student loan principal, so interest starts earning interest. New undergrad Direct Loans for July 2026 to June 2027 carry a fixed 6.52%; in a hypothetical $10,000 example with no payments for four years, capitalizing that interest (for example at consolidation) raises yearly interest from $652 to about $822. Since July 2023, Direct Loans no longer capitalize when you enter repayment or leave forbearance, but consolidation, some deferments ending and leaving IBR (older loans) still trigger it. Sources: US Department of Education (Federal Register, Nov 2022; FSA, June 2026), studentaid.gov.

News and education, not financial advice.
